samples.summary: cli.md documents the CLI flow's browser-binding cookie as `wafflebase_oauth_state`, but the implementation (and backend.md / rest-api.md) use `wafflebase_cli_state`. The whole point of the change is that the two flows must have *separate* names (github-auth.guard.ts:CLI_STATE_COOKIE, and backend.md's added paragraph explains why sharing one broke concurrent logins). The canonical CLI design doc therefore records the exact bug this change fixes as the design. Same error at cli.md:186 ("the backend sets a short-lived `wafflebase_oauth_state` cookie on that browser" in the CLI login-flow sequence).
samples.evidence: cli.md:234-237 "**Browser binding.** `GET /auth/github?mode=cli` sets a short-lived httpOnly `wafflebase_oauth_state` cookie" vs github-auth.guard.ts:`export const CLI_STATE_COOKIE = 'wafflebase_cli_state'` used by `issueLoginCookie(context, CLI_STATE_COOKIE)` for mode=cli.

samples.summary: cli.md still says the login state cookie is "`__Host-`-prefixed in production", while this change deliberately re-keys the prefix off the deployment scheme (`secureCookies()` returns true for any `https://` GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL, not just NODE_ENV=production) — and backend.md/rest-api.md were updated to say exactly that. The three top-level docs now disagree about the control that carries the whole cookie-planting defence.
samples.evidence: cli.md:236 "`__Host-`-prefixed in production" vs backend.md "it applies whenever `GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL` is `https://`".

samples.summary: `secretEquals` is defined twice in the same directory: privately in cli-auth.store.ts:55 and exported from github-auth.guard.ts:114, with byte-identical bodies. The exported one is already imported by auth.controller.ts, so the store's private copy is a straightforward duplication of an existing sibling helper (the repo's stated expectation is reuse).
samples.evidence: cli-auth.store.ts:55 `function secretEquals(a,b)` and github-auth.guard.ts:114 `export function secretEquals(a,b)` — same implementation.

samples.summary: Cookie/state plumbing shared by the guard *and* the controller (`loginCookieName`, `loginCookieOptions`, `secretEquals`, `stateSignature`, `bindingSecret`, `WEB_STATE_PREFIX`, three cookie-name constants) is exported out of a guard file. A guard is a request-pipeline component, not a shared-utility module; the controller now imports ten symbols from it. A small `auth/login-state.ts` (or similar) would be the right layer, and both docs describe these as a single "login cookie" concept.
samples.evidence: auth.controller.ts imports `bindingSecret, CLI_CONFIRM_PARAM, CliConsentRequest, GitHubAuthGuard, loginCookieName, CLI_STATE_COOKIE, loginCookieOptions, OAUTH_STATE_COOKIE, secretEquals, stateSignature, WEB_STATE_PREFIX` from './github-auth.guard'.

samples.summary: `SECRET_PATH_SEGMENTS` hard-codes the route topology of a different module (`share-links/:token/resolve`) inside the logging module. Route shape is owned by ShareLinkController; if that route is renamed or a second credential-in-path route is added, the redaction silently stops covering it with nothing to fail. A decorator/metadata-driven marker on the route (or a constant re-exported from the share-link module) would keep the two in one place.

Possible scope creep: the CLI error-envelope rework (`command` attribution across ~20 command files, `errorEnvelope`/`backendErrorEnvelope`, `ctx switch`/`schema`/`login` prose→envelope conversion, referenced in tests as "#661 follow-up") is an unrelated concern from the OAuth CSRF/PKCE/consent hardening that makes up the rest of the diff. Bundling two independent issues in one change makes the security-critical half harder to review and revert independently. Flagged as a suspicion since the originating issue text was not supplied.
samples.evidence: packages/cli/test/output.test.ts "#661 follow-up: `outputError` is not the only emitter" alongside backend OAuth state/PKCE changes in the same diff.

samples.summary: The new `/login?error=<reason>` contract (backend redirect target on a failed browser callback, plus the alert banner and `ERROR_MESSAGES` map in login-form.tsx) is documented on the backend side only. frontend.md describes the auth lifecycle and the `/login` route but was not updated with the query-param contract or the error-copy mapping, so the frontend doc no longer describes the shipped login page.
samples.evidence: backend.md adds "redirects to `FRONTEND_URL/login?error=login_state`"; frontend.md:45 still only lists `/login → Login` with no error-state contract.

samples.summary: The change makes previously-released CLI versions unable to log in at all (a `mode=cli` start without `nonce`/`code_challenge` is now a 400). That is a deliberate, documented break, but it is recorded only as prose inside the login-flow section of cli.md; there is no migration/compat note in rest-api.md's endpoint contract beyond "required", and no minimum-CLI-version statement. Worth an explicit compatibility/upgrade line so operators upgrading the backend know older CLIs break.
samples.evidence: cli.md "**Compatibility runs one way, and no longer runs at all for old clients.**" — the only place the break is stated.

verdict.reason: The quoted evidence checks out verbatim. docs/design/cli.md:234-237 documents the CLI flow's browser binding as a `wafflebase_oauth_state` cookie, and cli.md:186 repeats it in the CLI login sequence. The implementation uses a distinct cookie: github-auth.guard.ts:31 defines `CLI_STATE_COOKIE = 'wafflebase_cli_state'` with a comment stating it is deliberately NOT `OAUTH_STATE_COOKIE` because a shared name makes concurrent browser+CLI logins overwrite each other, and guard line 294 issues that cookie on the `mode=cli` path (line 302 uses OAUTH_STATE_COOKIE only for the browser flow). backend.md:122-123 and rest-api.md:339-342 both document `wafflebase_cli_state` for the CLI flow with the same rationale. The canonical CLI design doc therefore records the exact pre-change behavior the change removes, contradicting the implementation and the other two design docs. This is in-lane design-doc discipline (canonical subsystem doc not updated for the architecture change) and is a citable factual conflict, not a taste preference. No guard or corrective text elsewhere resolves it; cli-auth.store.ts:15 repeats the same stale name.
